findings.text: follow-on: load_claims_review_prompt and reckon/crew/prompts/claims_review.md are added but no production path or test calls the loader, so the prompt's CLAIM/CLAIM_SUMMARY grammar is held to the parser's _CLAIM_RE/_CLAIM_SUMMARY_RE by nothing; the landed-node prompt is pinned to the module's constants by tests/test_review_prompt_contract.py, and the claims prompt has no counterpart, so a rewrite of either side drifts silently.

follow-on: the manifest records its two suite observations as a prose tests line and a test_logs list and carries no baseline_suite/after_suite fields, so annotate_review_of_run resolves no base or head gate log for this run and yields an unmeasured added-failure count; the count was recoverable here (both gate-focused.log at 8dabe9100 and gate-promotion.log at 64c3a3938 reached their summary line, EXIT=0, with zero failing ids) but a reader on the production path sees it null.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit 8dabe9100 against base 64c3a3938; recovery_review_subject.py adds _INVESTIGATE_ROLE and four helpers plus a rubric branch in _review_dispatch_fields and _review_is_complete, review.py adds the claims constants, the two CLAIM regexes, the parser branch and the annotate early-return, claims_review.md is +54, and the test module is +221; nothing outside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names a temporary investigate run with a report and no commit composed with the claims rubric and no added_failure_count, a fixed three-CLAIM emission parsing to a complete record promotion accepts, and an implement run composed exactly as before; tests/test_a_read_only_run_gets_a_claims_review.py:126 composes the investigate case, :153 the brief-carried case, :170 the unchanged implement case, :180 drives the three CLAIM lines through parse_review and promotion_checks._require_review_waiver, and :211 the short-record incompleteness case; I re-ran the gate at head and read 48 passed, EXIT=0, and reproduced the negative control (role test removed -> the investigate case reddens, 1 failed 4 passed, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a review of a read-only run (role investigate, or a brief-carried node with no commit past its base) is composed with a claims rubric in place of the landed-node rubric, its stored record carrying claim verdicts and no suite-delta fields; _review_reads_a_report in recovery_review_subject.py:307 classifies such a run and _claims_review_done_when:333 composes the claims done-when, review.py:229 CLAIMS_RUBRIC/CLAIMS_REQUIRED drive the parser at review.py:652-716, _review_is_complete:790 measures a claims record on its own terms, and annotate_review_of_run:1830 returns it untouched, so the section's deliverable is met.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, one commit 8dabe9100, tests line naming the focused gate (48 passed, EXIT=0) and test_logs naming gate-focused.log and gate-promotion.log, negative_control_log ending EXIT=1; the manifest carries no baseline_suite/after_suite fields, so its suite delta is prose rather than the named pair a review is annotated from.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's declared paths and the diff; the four changed files (reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py, reckon/crew/review.py, reckon/crew/prompts/claims_review.md, tests/test_a_read_only_run_gets_a_claims_review.py) are all inside the declared write paths, and no fragment or figure was written, which the done-when does not name.

justifications.durability: the assertions are independent of the value under test — the investigate and brief cases red mid-composition when the role test is removed (proven), the three-CLAIM case parses a fixed literal emission, and the short-record case holds the CLAIMS_REQUIRED threshold so a one-claim record reads incomplete; the deduction is that load_claims_review_prompt (reckon/crew/review.py:437) and prompts/claims_review.md have no caller and no contract test, unlike load_review_prompt which tests/test_review_prompt_contract.py holds against the module's constants, so the prompt's CLAIM grammar can drift from _CLAIM_RE undetected.
justifications.evidence: I re-ran the focused gate at head 8dabe9100 (48 passed, EXIT=0) and independently reproduced the negative control in a scratch tree (role test removed -> tests/test_a_read_only_run_gets_a_claims_review.py:131 reddens, 1 failed 4 passed, EXIT=1), so the gate asserts the measure; the deduction is that the reviewed manifest records its suite observations as prose tests/test_logs lines and carries no baseline_suite/after_suite pair, so a reader following the production annotation path (annotate_review_of_run) sees an unmeasured count, and the added claims prompt is held by no falsifier.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's existing idiom — module-level constants with a rationale comment, disk-read prompt loaders beside the landed-node one, compiled CLAIM regexes beside _VERDICT_RE, and a rubric branch beside the plan/landed branches — and introduces no name the naming rules forbid; commit 8dabe9100 carries a conventional subject and a body with no plan label and no attribution.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the two clauses of the section's deliverable are both present — _review_reads_a_report (reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:307) returns True for role investigate and for a brief-carried node with no commit past its base, and the five other helpers carry the composition, the parse, the completeness measure and the annotate early-return, so a read-only run is reviewed on its claims and a landed implement run (this one) keeps the landed-node rubric.
justifications.reuse: no capability is forked — _review_reads_a_report reuses _pointer_role and _commits_beyond_base (reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py) rather than re-reading the pointer, _claims_review_is_complete extends _review_is_complete at its only call site, and the parser extends parse_review; I searched for a pre-existing claims/report rubric and found none.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff (reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py, reckon/crew/review.py, reckon/crew/prompts/claims_review.md, tests/test_a_read_only_run_gets_a_claims_review.py) is inside the manifest's declared write paths, the commit is a single conventional commit against base 64c3a3938, and nothing the goal does not imply was carried.
